title: Dependency scan record, version 3
description: Everything a revision scan found about one pinned commit of a subject repository. Every state is explicit: a gap, a failed lookup or an unavailable source is recorded, never left out.

ref.description: The ref as requested, before resolution.

url.description: The API base of a data source, such as endoflife.date.

fetched_at.description: When the data source was read.

source.description: subject: read from the scanned revision; trial: supplied for this run; none: no policy found, so every candidate is in scope.

consistency.description: Every logical dependency in the alias table, with the declarations the consistency check compared, so an alias nothing declares shows as such.

dependency.description: The logical dependency, such as the Go toolchain.

compared.description: The inventory entries whose declared versions were compared.

cross_checks.description: Direct dependencies a package manager reports as outdated where the scan has no matching candidate: a Renovate blind spot.

selection.description: What the scan would prepare, decided from the rest of the record and the defaults in use (update-selection).

id.description: Unique within the record; candidates and findings refer to it.

ecosystem.description: Package or source type, such as nuget, gomod, docker, github-actions, pypi, bicep-module.

current.description: Current version or constraint as declared; null when it can't be determined.

origin.description: declared: written in a manifest; locked: resolved in a lock file.

locked_because.description: Why the scan lists a locked entry, given exactly for those: drift, the lock file resolves an older version than the repository declares (design decision 3a); vulnerability, an advisory concerns a package only a lock file or an indirect module has.

state.description: current: lookup succeeded, nothing newer; outdated: candidates exist; unknown: lookup failed; skipped: not looked up, see reason.

basis.description: advisory_fix: no registry was asked; the dependency's candidates are the fixed versions its advisories name, which need not be the newest. Absent when the state comes from a lookup.

held_by.description: The policy rule that holds the candidate.

group.description: The group the policy's group rules put the candidate in, by its groupName. Absent when no group rule matches it. Recorded whether or not the candidate is held.

basis.description: advisory_fix: the fixed version an advisory on the dependency names, added by the scan rather than found by a lookup, so not necessarily the newest version. Absent when a lookup found it, or, for lock drift, when it is the version the repository declares.

released_at.description: When the source published this version, in UTC. Absent when the source publishes no date, and always for an advisory fix.

fixed_version.description: null when the advisory names no fixed version.

last_affected.description: The advisory's last affected version, when it states that instead of a fixed version: a fix exists, and any version above this one has it.

fix_reached_by_candidate.description: Whether an in-scope update candidate of the dependency is outside the advisory; unknown when its lookup failed or the advisory's ranges can't be evaluated. Present whenever a fixed or last affected version is.

fix_reached_by.description: The versions of the in-scope candidates outside the advisory's affected ranges, in version order: those that reach the fix. Present whenever fix_reached_by_candidate is true or false, and empty exactly when it is false.

fix_held_by.description: The policy rule holding the only candidates that reach the fix.

dependabot_alerts.description: Open Dependabot alerts, by number, on the same advisory and package: a second source that agrees. They describe the default branch, not necessarily the scanned commit (see dependabot_alerts).

The repository's open Dependabot alerts, as a comparison source. Present only when they were read; otherwise a gap with subject dependabot-alerts says why, and the record claims nothing about them. They describe the default branch as Dependabot last analysed it, not necessarily the scanned commit.

ref.description: The default branch, which the alerts describe.

commit.description: The branch's head, read just before the alerts.

is_scanned_commit.description: Whether that head is the scanned commit. When it isn't, a difference between the alerts and the scan may be the branch's, not a miss of the scan.

ecosystem.description: As Dependabot names it, such as go or nuget.

manifest.description: The file Dependabot found the package in.

dependency.description: The inventory entry for the same package in the same file, when the scan has one.

fixed_version.description: Dependabot's first patched version; null when there is none.

result.description: matched: a vulnerability in this record has the same advisory on the same package, in the alert's manifest or a file beside it, and lists the alert; matched_elsewhere: only vulnerabilities in other files do, such as a central version, and they list it; unmatched: none does.

lifecycle.description: One version line in use, with every inventory entry that uses it. An image or runtime declaration without a mapping to lifecycle data is listed under its own name, as unknown.

product.description: The endoflife.date product, such as go, dotnet, python, alpine-linux, debian; for an entry without a mapping, its own name.

line.description: The version line in use as the product names it, such as 1.25 or 10; the declared value when it names no line.

end_of_life.description: The date support ends or ended, when one is published.

supported_lines.description: The lines still supported on the scan's date, oldest first.

source.description: Where the lifecycle data came from.

dependencies.description: The inventory entries that use the line, with locations in the same order.

then.description: Ended without a published date: the reason says so.

dependency.description: The logical dependency, such as the Go toolchain.
The inventory entry that makes this declaration, with the value as declared.

version.description: The version read from the declared value, such as 1.27 from golang:1.27-alpine.

subject.description: The file, or the data source (such as dependabot-alerts), that couldn't be covered.

date.description: The scan's date in UTC, which the batch window and release ages are measured against.

batch_window.description: The days of every month, inclusive, when batch updates are selected.

minimum_release_age_days.description: How old a batch update's release must be, in days, on the scan's date.

next_opens.description: The first day of the next window, after the month of the scan's date.

units.description: What to prepare, with the reasons, targets and evidence.

not_prepared.description: Every reason that didn't become a unit, and why.

dependency.description: The inventory entry the update changes.

current.description: The entry's current version, as the inventory has it.

version.description: The version of an in-scope candidate of the dependency.

released_at.description: When the candidate was published; absent when the source publishes no date.

age_days.description: Whole days from the release to the scan's date; negative for a release dated after it; unknown exactly when there is no release date.

name.description: Safe to use as a branch name as it is; stable across scans for the same unit.

name_collision.description: The name was changed to tell it apart from another unit whose name was the same.

subject.description: A group, a package or a version line: what the unit's name comes from.

breaking.description: A lifecycle move, or any major target.

kind.description: fix_held: vulnerable, but only candidates the policy holds reach the fix; no_route: no fixed version is recorded; no_candidate: no in-scope candidate reaches the fix; early_warning: a line is ending but no in-scope candidate leaves it; not_evaluated: data the decision needs is missing; waiting: a batch update too young for this window.

reason.description: The reason the update would have been selected for.

detail.description: Why it wasn't prepared, in words.
